extracted.intended_audience: patent office staff and IP / R&D professionals evaluating commercial IP database platforms
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating or using a commercial IP intelligence platform (Patsnap) for patent novelty/invalidity searching, image/design searching, AI-agentic workflows, and data-security/privacy considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data coverage (patents and related records)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantitative coverage of datasets: Patent 191M (172 jurisdictions), Scientific Literature 192M, Legal 2.7B, News 26M, Chemical Structure 250M, Material Properties 250M, SEP 185M, OneID 130M, Research Reports 834K, M&A 1.5M, Government Funding 4M, Tdoc 1.5M; 320+ patent fields, 430+ innovation indicator fields, 20 categories and 3.5B+ patent and R&D records with daily update.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High breadth and depth across patent and non-patent sources is presented as a quality criterion; daily updates and large jurisdictional coverage (172) are highlighted as advantages for comprehensive searches and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain-specific LLM accuracy / verified references
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of an IP-domain-specific LLM (PatsnapGPT) to reduce hallucinations and return real, verified patent references instead of made-up or incorrect references from general LLMs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: searching for patents on 'biodegradable golf tees' — PatsnapGPT returns verifiable patent numbers whereas generic LLMs may hallucinate. Domain specificity is positioned as a key criterion to trustability of generated prior-art citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data security and privacy commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: Patsnap will not collect users' privacy data for large model training; customer prompts and data will not be used for model training; customer data encrypted at rest using AES256; data transmission encrypted using TLS1.3; collection of customer information is disclosed in privacy agreement; customer consent obtained; customer owns input/output data; customers can choose data retention duration; data will not be passed to third parties; LLM will not collect personal privacy data and sensitive information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are explicit operational and contractual commitments that should be used as evaluation criteria when selecting an IP platform: encryption standards, ownership, consent, retention choices, and assurances about training-data usage are all called out.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI agent autonomy vs AI tools (mode of assistance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinction between 'AI Tools Mode' (user completes most work; AI provides information for some tasks) and 'AI Agent Mode' (AI completes most work: decomposes tasks, selects tools, controls progress; user sets goal, provides resources, monitors results).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate platforms by the level of automation and autonomy offered: agentic workflows intended to complete full workflows versus tools that require manual orchestration by the user.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty Search — Semantic Search (precision metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Semantic Search finds the most similar technical solutions globally; Top 100 accuracy when identifying English X documents reaches 78%. Scope: search over >192M patents and 192M scientific articles using English or Chinese input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Semantic search quality is measured by 'Top 100 accuracy' (probability of hitting X/affecting-novelty documents within top 100 results). Users can customize semantic inputs by adding/removing concept words to focus results. Platform claims a hybrid approach (traditional word-vector models + generative LLM semantic understanding) to reach higher precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semantic Top-100 Accuracy definition and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Semantic Top 100 Accuracy: using a patent number for semantic search, the probability of hitting X documents affecting novelty in the top 100 search results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explicit metric is presented as a scoring/quality indicator for semantic search effectiveness and should be used to compare semantic-search performance across products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty Search — Image Search (design & technical drawings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Image Search finds visually similar design patents (physical images) and conceptually similar line drawings across >20M global design patents with TOP100 accuracy up to 73.7%; image search for technology enables searching >30M utility model patent drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality criteria include background-noise filtering, multi-image search capability, coverage of design and utility-model drawings, and reported TOP100 accuracy (probability of finding invalidity evidence in top 100). Use cases: protecting design patents and identifying similar appearances across markets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty Search — Field Search and Patent DNA (deep-processed fields)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent DNA transcribes and refines obscure patent text into searchable fields/AI summaries (e.g., technical problems, technical benefits). Field Search offers >250 search fields (text, classification, companies, references & family, patent status & quality, legal events, national-specific fields, workspace and corporate-customized fields).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deep-processed, domain-specific fields and AI transcription are positioned as a quality criterion to improve precision and reduce recall noise. Patent DNA currently covers China, the USA, and Europe over the past decade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semantic Filtering for screening
rubrics_metrics.description: Semantic Filtering restricts search results to a specific batch and identifies/sorts by semantic similarity from high to low so the key patents closest to the technical solution appear first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a screening criterion, semantic filtering reduces the need for manually reading large result sets by prioritizing semantically closest documents, improving screening quality and efficiency compared to fixed/faceted filters alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family and citation expansion and correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Family data covers 172 patent offices and 192M patents' application numbers, priority rights, PCT applications, EP entries to designated countries, continuation/divisional applications, double applications in one case, etc. Patsnap reanalyzes family relationships to identify and correct erroneously associated families, increasing coverage versus INPADOC. Citation data covers 61 patent offices and includes source of citations, applicants, citations from examination documents, citation types (X/Y/A), US classes 102/103, non-patent citations, and differentiation between self-citations and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive, corrected family/citation data is a criterion for completeness of prior-art linkage and for avoiding missed relevant comparisons during novelty searches; superior family coverage is highlighted as an advantage over INPADOC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty Search Agent — multi-strategy generation and workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: The AI Novelty Search Agent automatically breaks a provided technical description into technical features, generates multiple search strategies (semantic search, classification search, 4x keyword searches including synonyms, AI field search, hypernyms & hyponyms), family & citation search, retrieves most relevant prior art, generates comparison tables and a final report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation should include whether the agent produces multiple complementary search strategies, iterative searches mirroring human-led search depth, and the extent to which the agent automates end-to-end novelty-search steps to save time and cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty Search Agent — report contents and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent output: comprehensive final report containing Overview & Title, a breakdown of the Inventive Features of the Solution, Extracted Technical Features, a Technical Feature Comparison Table (input vs top matches), Overall Reference Comparison with a Similarity Score, clear Summary of findings, Appendix 1: Technical Elements & Synonyms, and Appendix 2: Search Strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency and reproducibility are emphasized as evaluation criteria — inclusion of extracted features, comparison tables, similarity scoring, and appendices documenting search strategy and synonyms supports defensibility of the search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenge awareness for search quality (anti-patterns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identified challenges include: semantic algorithms or incomplete data coverage leading to low relevance and time-consuming novelty checking; image searches suffering from incomplete global data coverage and low precision; missing search fields or use of common keywords causing high-recall noisy results; and manually reading many patents is time-consuming and prone to omissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These challenges serve as anti-patterns to check for in vendor claims; evaluate how a platform addresses each (algorithm sophistication, dataset completeness, deep fields, semantic filtering) rather than accepting claims at face value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive deep-processed fields and AI transcription as a quality differentiator
rubrics_metrics.description: Patsnap claims exclusive high-quality deep-processed patent fields and AI transcription capabilities (Patent DNA) to make it easier to find relevant comparison documents and improve novelty/invalidity search quality and efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing platforms, verify the existence, scope, and accuracy of deep-processed fields and AI transcriptions and whether they materially improve precision over raw-text search and standard classification-based approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage and precision metrics presented as product KPIs
rubrics_metrics.description: Product-level KPIs are provided as claims: Semantic Top100 Accuracy 78% (English X documents), Image Search TOP100 Accuracy 73.7%, multi-million to billion scale dataset counts, and jurisdictional coverage numbers (172 offices, 61 offices for citations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These KPIs should be validated and benchmarked in procurement/evaluation: methodology for deriving 'Top100 accuracy', test corpora, and definitions (what counts as X documents, test cases) are necessary to accept claimed metrics.
